summary: Round-24 plan check, 06:40-06:55Z on 28 Sep. At the 06:32:32Z poll header, probes 47, 48, 49 and 50 are all PENDING. LB snapshot 0639Z: our team is #179 at 0.956, count 48, 9th of 56 in the block, k = 8. No E10 trigger: the feed shows the best public notebook at 0.953; the x138 author's team went 0.956 -> 0.957 from a 00:03Z submission; kunaldesale2408 re-ran its notebook at 06:37Z. The exp86a/b/c notebooks are built correctly: their knob lines come after the x138 defaults. The plan has six concrete defects. (1) The last 28 Sep slot is decided at 12:00Z, but probe 50 (exp85a, the one lever with a public track record) becomes terminal only at ~12:27-12:51Z; the decision should wait for that read. (2) The 743929 knob pair has no lever code, no BASE membership and no lookup row, so exp86a and exp86b have no legal slot. exp86c (READMIT 0.92) is a knob rung, which v2 (6) and W4 AMEND 2 (4) ban in W3/W4. (3) The BASE=exp85a branch has no CI or SEC stack builds. Named exp87*, they would fall into the wrong ledger family (safetail instead of safetail_ci) and outside R8 COVERAGE. (4) The E10 SI runbook fails its own gate whenever BASE is a knob file; this was confirmed by a read-only gate run. (5) The exp86a/b dummy gate is not pre-registered beyond a scratchpad script. An exact node-row identity with exp85a is available. (6) The user was active at 04:32-04:39Z, so the open questions (02:00Z cap lift on 29 Sep, Q3) can be asked now; the lift would allow an informed W5 before the finals read. No new mechanism is proposed, and no closed family is reopened.

findings.what: The last 28 Sep slot (W2b, 12:00Z) is decided ~30-50 min before probe 50 (exp85a) can read. exp85a was submitted at 05:02:30Z; K2-family latency is 7.4-7.8 h, so it becomes terminal at ~12:27-12:51Z. The 743929 knobs are the only lever with an outside public record (+0.001 each on an x138 fork). If 50 reads '+', the best use of the slot is the DIV+K stack (exp86a/exp86b) or a K-based stack, and none of these can be chosen blind at 12:00Z ('never stack an unread lever in W2'). The CONTEXT text is also inconsistent. The 04:38Z amendment moves exp80a/exp81 to W3/W4, but the 06:26Z entry puts exp81 back into W2b through W2 v4 (2). W2 v4 (2)(v) already allows the slot to move to W3 (<= 23:30Z), so waiting costs nothing. A file submitted by 13:30Z reads ~20:30-21:20Z (non-CI), still before the W4 builds and dummies.

READ TABLE v3 (1) codes files only against exp70g, and v3 (5)'s BASE order (exp70g > exp78a > exp78b > exp80a > exp70q) has no exp85a. The W2 v4 (4) lookup and W4 AMEND 2 (1) 'FULL = BASE + every + lever' list only CI/SEC/DIV rows. Separately, exp86c (READMIT 0.92, 'the next step down if 50 is +') is a knob rung. v2 (6) ('Never in W3/W4: knob rungs', l.3170) and W4 AMEND 2 (4) ('Never: knob/thr/... rungs', l.3373) ban it. It is also not a disclosed value, so aggressive mode does not cover it. The lab prior points the wrong way: readmitted nodes match GT at ~1% (73/13,284), the [0.94, 0.965) band has 0 candidates near GT, and the node term is linear (+0.84% nodes at 0.94 ~ -0.0008). Submitting exp86c or exp86a/b without a line written now would be a post-hoc rule change after the 50 read.

findings.what: The BASE = exp85a branch has no stack builds. If 50 is + and neither DIV rung is +, the next files are exp85a + CI and exp85a + n2a SEC, and neither exists. Numbering is a trap. Under the next free names (exp87*), tools/runtime_ledger.py would put a CI stack in family safetail (deadline 9.5 h, insertion gate 8.0 h) instead of safetail_ci (10.75 h / 10.2 h), and the insertion-gate reading and V_pub eligibility would be wrong. The R8 COVERAGE pre-submit line names 'the CI stacks exp83*' and 'the SEC stacks exp82*', so exp87* would also fail the 'this line is present' check.

Name them exp83h = exp85a + coordinject a0.5 3 um and exp82d = exp85a + n2a secondary 7029fe69, so the existing ledger rule and R8 COVERAGE apply unchanged. findings.what: The E10 SI runbook fails its own gate whenever BASE is a knob file (exp85a/exp86a/exp86b). Runbook section 9 builds K from the BASE probe.json filtered to DIVINS_* keys, so the SI carries no ILP/READMIT lines, but it gates with REF = $BASE_DIR. A read-only gate run with REF = exp85a and a knob-free cap-6 SI FAILs notebook-bytes. Passing the knobs is not a fix either: tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base succ accepts only SUCC_KNOBS, which exclude ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT and READMIT_MIN_SCORE, and the builder's own INFO says a successor whose READMIT differs from 0.965 should prefer the K1 recipe. A successor notebook may also have tuned READMIT itself.
